newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cyprus seen buying 25,000 T barley near $152/tn.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus seen buying 25,000 T barley near $152/tn.

text.p: Cyprus was seen close to buying 25,000 tonnes of barley on Friday, a deal that could work out near $152 per tonne, European grain traders said.
The estimated price includes both cost and freight.
Cyprus was tendering for 25,000 tonnes of barley from any origin for shipment by May 20.
Grain traders said official results were not yet available but the barley was expected to go for just under $152 per tonne.
Although the origin is optional, this would imply a French price of around $138 per tonne fob, one barley expert said.
French domestic prices have risen steadily from around $130 per tonne earlier this month mainly on tighter supplies in northern ports and strong export activity.
The European Commission rejected bids for barley export subsidies on Thursday, along with those for all other gains, citing worries the domestic market was overheating.
EU barley export tenders remain open officially until May 29, though the season for giving out licences may effectively end sooner, perhaps next week, traders and officials said.

Latest figures show the EU has committed 6.069 million tonnes of barley for export this July/June season, over 4.6 times the 1.3 million tonnes awarded by the same date last year. -- Tim Hepher, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
